solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sadly it's said cruel leader could be thus

definitions.text: Sadly it's said cruel leader could be thus

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of the words before it are put in a sorry new order
the leader of a word is its opening letter, here taken from cruel

explanation.surface: A grim remark that a tyrant at the head of things might be given to cruelty for its own sake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges IT'S SAID into SADISTI; 'leader' takes the C of cruel. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a cruel leader could be this.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enjoys inflicting pain is exactly what a cruel ruler could be described as.

clue.text: Steal elk for butchering, being thus?

definitions.text: Steal elk for butchering, being thus?

indicators.note: butchering cuts things up, so the letters of the words before it are chopped and rearranged

explanation.surface: Poaching an elk for meat leaves nothing but bones behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for butchering' rearranges STEAL ELK; the whole clue is also the definition, since a butchered elk ends up as a bare frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcass stripped of its meat is reduced to bones, the state of a creature that is all frame.

clue.text: Artist's studio could be an entertaining place

definitions.meaning: playfully, a room where someone draws pictures
the formal reception room of a house where guests are received

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is whimsical: a studio is a room for drawing. The real sense is the old-fashioned British parlour where visitors are entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal sitting room for receiving guests is the traditional place for entertaining at home.

clue.text: Hugely ill-mannered sort involved in new pub arrest

indicators.note: new says the letters of the words that follow are made into something fresh, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A very rude customer gets caught up in a fresh arrest at the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges PUB ARREST; 'involved in' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A super brat is an exceptionally badly behaved person, the prefix intensifying a word for a rude child.

clue.text: Hopeless Time writer I sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the assembled letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A despairing writer admits sending off the pages too late, beaten by the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns T + PEN + I upside down in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone clumsy and incompetent at a task is hopeless at it; the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Pressure will break tired principal

indicators.note: P breaks into the word for tired, splitting it open

parts.note: stale, as in worn out or jaded
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Stress will finally crack an exhausted head teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will break' puts P inside STALE. 'principal' looks like a noun (a head teacher) but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple product or food is the main, chief one, as with a principal item.

clue.text: Path leads to terribly riotous trouble

indicators.note: the leads of words are their first letters, taken here from terribly and riotous

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A road that ends in serious disorder and unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' takes the first letters of terribly and riotous, TR, then trouble gives AIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a track or route through country, the same thing as a path.

clue.text: Secretary gets with husband and I'm disgusted!

parts.note: PA, a personal assistant

explanation.surface: A wife exclaims in disgust that the office assistant has taken up with her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection expresses contempt or disgust, the same feeling the exclamation voices.

clue.text: Flapper feels bad about robbing banks

indicators.note: robbing the banks takes away the outer edges of the word, both its first and last letters

parts.note: regrets, is sorry about

explanation.surface: A 1920s flapper is ashamed of her bank robberies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'robbing banks' strips the outer letters R and S from REGRETS. 'Flapper' suggests a jazz-age girl but means something that flaps its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron-like bird beats its wings in flight, so it is playfully a flapper.

clue.text: Second-rate celebs can be annoying people

definitions.meaning: an informal term for irritating people, sores that rub you the wrong way

explanation.walkthrough: Split as B-LISTERS for the first sense; the second is informal slang for pests.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesser celebrities are the B-list, and pests who chafe like sores on the skin are called this informally.

clue.text: Old politician puts on brew for model

parts.note: ex, meaning former

indicators.note: the brew is put on around the politician, like a garment wrapping him

parts.note: ale, a brewed beer
MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A retired politician gains weight from drinking beer, or puts the kettle on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts on' reads like gaining weight or brewing up, but here the brew is worn around the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a specimen or pattern to copy, which is what a model is.

clue.text: Material in article must be screened by king

indicators.note: being screened by something means being hidden inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Lear, Shakespeare's tragic king
the, the definite article

explanation.surface: Something in a newspaper piece has to be censored by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be screened by' sounds like censorship; here it means hidden inside. The king is Shakespeare's, not a real monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanned hide is a material used for shoes, belts and upholstery.

clue.text: Record label, to get good taxes, relocates abroad

parts.note: EMI, the British record company
rates are British local property taxes

explanation.surface: A record company moves overseas to obtain better tax treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave one's country to settle in another is to move abroad for good.

clue.text: The answer to this clue is window

definitions.meaning: in crossword jargon, each grid entry is called by this name
a pane or opening that lets in daylight

explanation.walkthrough: Crossword makers call each answer slot in the grid by this name, so the clue refers to itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A window pane is traditionally termed this, and setters use the same word for any grid entry.

clue.text: I study trees and gloat seeing larks around

indicators.note: larking around is playing about, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tree expert admits to smirking while watching songbirds flit about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'larks around' rearranges GLOAT SEEING. 'trees' are family trees, not forests, and 'larks' are not birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A family historian researches family trees, the ancestry charts of a lineage.

clue.text: Park warden loses head, displaying this?

definitions.text: Park warden loses head, displaying this?

indicators.note: losing its head means the opening letter is taken off

parts.note: a ranger looks after a park or forest

explanation.surface: A park keeper flies into a rage; is this the emotion on show?
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' drops R from RANGER; losing your head is also what one does in this mood, so the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing one's head, in the sense of losing self-control, shows rage.

clue.text: Infringement that's just coming to light

definitions.meaning: the violation of a rule or law, as in the breach of a contract
of news, newly emerging as it happens

explanation.definitionFit: A breach of a rule is its violation, and news that is just emerging is described with the same word.

clue.text: Support team that's behind

parts.note: back, to support
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A reserve team that is trailing in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like an adjective about the score but is the noun for the rump.
explanation.definitionFit: The behind is the buttocks, the part of the body one sits on.

clue.text: Take note of figures seen in Castle Dracula?

parts.note: a keep is the strongest tower of a castle
Count Dracula, the vampire noble

explanation.surface: Someone keeping track of the numbers seen at a vampire's castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' suggests visitors seen in the castle, but means numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a running tally is to note numbers as they mount up.

clue.text: Can southern belle finally finish unfinished business?

parts.note: can is slang for a lavatory, as is loo

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of belle

parts.note: end

explanation.surface: Can a southern belle wrap up her outstanding affairs at last?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as a verb but is the noun for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail left unresolved, a matter still to be tied up, is one hanging thread.

clue.text: Associates of criminals full of discretion

indicators.note: the criminals are filled with discretion, so it sits inside them

parts.note: cons, short for convicts
tact, delicacy in dealing with others

explanation.surface: The partners of crooks are very discreet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Associates of' tempts as a single phrase, but 'of' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Associates are people one knows and can call on, a network of useful acquaintances.

clue.text: Some sneer at old and inspiring female

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people mock the old and the inspirational woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'and' in the definition; it is only a link between the wordplay and 'inspiring female', a muse.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Greek Muse of love poetry, one of the goddesses who inspire artists.

clue.text: Office worker and a male engaged in row

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so one letter is set inside the other word

parts.note: din, a loud noise or racket

explanation.surface: An office clerk and a man involved in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged in' puts M inside DIN, after A. 'row' means noise, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Administrative staff handle paperwork in an office, informally called by this shortening.

clue.text: When one's soon to get hitched in white

parts.note: as, meaning when, as in 'as I arrived'
a hen, a bride-to-be celebrating on her hen night

explanation.surface: A bride about to marry dresses in white.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is the British pre-wedding night out for the bride; 'white' suggests the dress but means pale.
explanation.definitionFit: A face drained of colour from shock or illness is grey-pale, deathly white.

clue.text: Earl welcomed by pleasant relation

indicators.note: being welcomed by something means being taken in, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: nice

explanation.surface: A nobleman is warmly received by a kind family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomed by' puts E inside NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family relative.

clue.text: Awfully asocial American is coarse

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of the word after it are rearranged

parts.note: US, the United States

explanation.surface: An unsociable American is described as crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' looks like an intensifier for 'asocial' but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd, smutty talk is crude or vulgar, the sense of coarse here.

clue.text: After leaving force, brief is serving up Whoppers

indicators.note: after the force leaves, its letter is removed from the word

parts.note: flying, as in a flying visit, a brief one
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A lawyer quits the police and starts selling burgers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After leaving' takes F out of FLYING. 'brief' looks like a lawyer, 'Whoppers' like burgers.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoppers are big lies, so telling them is fibbing, being dishonest.

clue.text: Fiery type books into hotel by promontory

indicators.note: the books go into the hotel, checking in after its letter

parts.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
OT, the Old Testament books of the Bible
a head or headland juts out into the sea

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered guest checks into a hotel by a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quick-tempered and impetuous is a fiery person.

clue.text: One who sings about one on board?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rat is an informer, someone who sings to the police

explanation.surface: A singer performs about someone on a ship or a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: To sing is slang for informing; 'on board' means aboard ship, a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar is an old name for a sailor, someone serving aboard ship.

clue.text: At home, posh roofing material is not worth using

parts.note: in, at home
U, upper-class usage in British English
a tile covers roofs

explanation.surface: An upper-crust house with expensive roof tiles turns out to be pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were labels for upper-class and non-upper-class British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare adjective means useless, of no practical value.

clue.text: Annoyed the Queen comes in wearing nothing

indicators.note: comes in says one letter enters the other word

parts.note: naked
R, for Regina

explanation.surface: Irritated that the monarch walks in nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Queen' gives only R (Regina), not ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Narked is British slang for irritated or peeved.

clue.text: A crowd gathering round relations daughter upset

indicators.note: the crowd gathers round, enclosing the relations inside it

parts.note: a gate is the crowd attending a sports match
it, a euphemism for sex, as in sexual relations

explanation.surface: A crowd surrounds the relatives while a daughter is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' looks like family but is the euphemism for sex; 'gate' is a sporting attendance figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To be agitated is to be troubled and nervous, the same as upset.
